Owner: PhD Jonathan MERCIER · Type: epic
Created: 2026-11-19 · Updated: 2026-11-19

DESCRIPTION

  Goal: pull-based, WIP-limited delivery loop with rolling-wave (just-in-time)
  planning, so agents finish work instead of spreading effort across epics.   
  Goals: G1 finish started work (Done or explicit blocker) before pulling new 
  work. G2 focus agent context on one epic and one batch. G3 create detailed  
  tasks only for near-term work.                                              
  Non-goals: automatic closure without DoD evidence/authority; automatic      
  session launch, commit or push; replacing Beads as task truth.              
  Requirements:                                                               
  FR-1 Single active epic: only tasks of the epic in delivery are pulled;     
  switching needs an explicit user decision.                                  
  FR-2 WIP = active batch: only batch tasks are in_progress; nothing else     
  claimed or left half-open.                                                  
  FR-3 Batch selection: batch = all ready, unblocked tasks of the active epic 
  that can run independently, bounded only by the host's subagent concurrency 
  limit (e.g. Goose's configured maximum); Skills never set or override a cap.
  Independent tasks run in parallel subagents with disjoint writable paths.   
  FR-4 Finish before pull: no task outside the batch is pulled until the batch
  closes or a blocker is reported.                                            
  FR-5 DoD-gated closure: close only after Test evidence + Judge accepted +   
  current closure authority; otherwise stay open with named blocker and       
  restart action.                                                             
  FR-6 No speculative tasks: epics not next in line keep goal, outcomes, rough
  scope only, no child tasks.                                                 
  FR-7 Just-in-time refinement: when the active epic has no ready tasks for   
  the next batch, automatically propose Research->Plan refinement for it (or  
  the next epic in order); horizon one batch ahead; tracker writes only with  
  tracker-write authority.                                                    
  FR-8 Discovered work: recorded as open follow-up linked discovered-from     
  source; never claimed nor added to the batch.                               
  Decisions (user, 2026-11-19): D1 no plugin cap, host concurrency limit      
  governs; D2 refine one batch ahead; D3 automatic proposal, writes need      
  authority; D4 blocked task is unclaimed back to open with named blocker,    
  rest of batch continues; D5 disjoint paths by default, worktree only on     
  collision and with authority.                                               
  Change rule: loop/route/tool changes update docs/skill-flow.md and          
  tests/test_skill_flow.py together.

content.text:
Treat roadmap outcomes, epic capabilities, user-story behavior and executable tasks
   as different levels. Keep distant work coarse and detail the ready frontier only.
   Keep exactly one active epic across runs and sessions; an epic may need several runs.
   Pull work only from its descendants (`bd ready --parent <epic>`). Switch the active
   epic only on an explicit user decision, never because another epic has ready work.
   Work in progress is the active batch: only its tasks are claimed or in_progress.
   The coordinator owns the batch and each worker owns one task, not one phase or commit.
   Give each task one primary deliverable and its exit criteria; each action or contribution
   must serve it or follow an explicit authorized objective switch. Do not start
   several tasks sequentially and leave them in progress: multiple active tasks
   require actual active workers with distinct assignments, not intended delegation.
   Distinguish planned/selected work, verified claims and observed execution in the
   existing tracker/checkpoint; a claim alone proves neither a running delegate nor
   permission. Keep contributions under their batch task unless independently resumable
   outcomes require separate authorized tickets; no ticket per file or phase.
   Before writes, verify that the task ID leads to goal, requirement, scope, dependencies,
   checks and restart context. In Beads, parents express hierarchy, blocking edges express
   prerequisites; claim is not a file lock. Repair missing task context, not a second tracker.

   When the active epic has no ready tasks for the next batch, propose Research → Plan
